clinician.final_diagnosis: Ileo-ileal intussusception secondary to a T3N1 neuroendocrine tumor (NET), grade 1
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man with a history of peptic ulcer disease and chronic NSAID use (daily Goody's powder) presented to the ED with a 2-day history of hematemesis, maroon-colored stools, and lower abdominal pain, accompanied by palpitations and shortness of breath that resolved upon arrival. Vital signs were stable on presentation. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness across the lower abdomen. Initial laboratory work showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, hematocrit 36%), with other labs unremarkable. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast identified an ileo-ileal intussusception in the right lower quadrant with irregular mucosal/submucosal thickening distal to the intussuscepted segment, suspicious for an underlying small bowel mass, without signs of intestinal obstruction. The patient was taken to the operating room for exploratory laparotomy, where a small bowel mass was identified approximately 30 cm from the ileocecal valve, serving as the lead point for the intussusception. A palpable lymph node was noted in the associated mesentery. Approximately 15 cm of small bowel and 13 lymph nodes (including the palpable node) were resected and sent for pathological analysis. No liver abnormalities were noted. The postoperative course was complicated by an ileus that resolved with conservative management. The resected specimen was pathologically confirmed to be a neuroendocrine tumor with grade 1 histology and TNM staging of T3N1.

final.final_diagnosis: Ileo-ileal intussusception secondary to a T3N1 neuroendocrine tumor (NET), grade 1
final.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man with a history of peptic ulcer disease and chronic NSAID use (daily Goody's powder) presented to the ED with a 2-day history of hematemesis, maroon-colored stools, and lower abdominal pain, accompanied by palpitations and shortness of breath that resolved upon arrival. Vital signs were stable on presentation. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness across the lower abdomen. Initial laboratory work showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL, hematocrit 36%), with other labs unremarkable. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast identified an ileo-ileal intussusception in the right lower quadrant with irregular mucosal/submucosal thickening distal to the intussuscepted segment, suspicious for an underlying small bowel mass, without signs of intestinal obstruction. The patient was taken to the operating room for exploratory laparotomy, where a small bowel mass was identified approximately 30 cm from the ileocecal valve, serving as the lead point for the intussusception. A palpable lymph node was noted in the associated mesentery. Approximately 15 cm of small bowel and 13 lymph nodes (including the palpable node) were resected and sent for pathological analysis. No liver abnormalities were noted. The postoperative course was complicated by an ileus that resolved with conservative management. The resected specimen was pathologically confirmed to be a neuroendocrine tumor with grade 1 histology and TNM staging of T3N1.
